items.editor_note: Proposes separating memory types and aligning them, targeting entangled information in conversational memory.

editorial.tldr: Early threads covered evaluating agent memory beyond the context window and invalidating stale entries (PACMI, Oct 5). On Oct 11 an open-source repo showed coding-agent memory as a tree of plain files.
editorial.whats_new: ETAMem (Oct 27) splits heterogeneous memory types and aligns them for conversational agents, following ActionRAG (Oct 23), which retrieves relation-consistent evidence via graph diffusion.
editorial.why_it_matters: Memory research is moving from simple stores to structured retrieval: relation-aware evidence (ActionRAG) and separated memory types (ETAMem). Both add moving parts you would have to run, test and version.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before adopting a structured memory design, rerun it on your own long-conversation traces and compare against a plain retrieval baseline; both new papers are unreplicated preprints.

status.detail: Memory work now spans lightweight file stores and two new arXiv papers on structured retrieval; all are preprints or repos without independent replication.

open_questions: Does PACMI's invalidation cascade hold up on an independent long-horizon agent benchmark?
Will any file-based memory store publish results on stale-memory handling?
Do ActionRAG or ETAMem release code and benchmark numbers others can reproduce?
